-- List operations by pattern matching

myLength :: [a] -> Int
myLength []     = 0
myLength (_:xs) = 1 + myLength xs

mySum :: Num a => [a] -> a
mySum []     = 0
mySum (x:xs) = x + mySum xs

myMap :: (a -> b) -> [a] -> [b]
myMap _ []     = []
myMap f (x:xs) = f x : myMap f xs

myFilter :: (a -> Bool) -> [a] -> [a]
myFilter _ []     = []
myFilter p (x:xs)
    | p x       = x : myFilter p xs
    | otherwise =     myFilter p xs

-- Test in GHCi:
-- myLength [1,2,3,4,5]  => 5
-- mySum [1..10]          => 55
-- myMap (*2) [1..5]      => [2,4,6,8,10]
-- myFilter even [1..10]  => [2,4,6,8,10]
description: Pattern matching chooses an equation from the shape of a value. You handle an empty list separately from a head and tail.

steps.description: myLength returns zero for an empty list. For a nonempty list, it counts one and recurses on the tail xs.
mySum adds the head x to the sum of the tail. Num requires an element type that supports arithmetic.
myMap takes a function f and applies it to each head. The colon operator puts that result before the recursively mapped tail.
A guard is a condition after |. myFilter keeps x when p x is true and continues with xs in either case.
These comments pair sample calls with their stated results. You can compare each call with the definition above it.
